validated_results.reason: Arginine and other GPRC6A ligands were tested only in prostate cancer cell lines and in Gprc6a-/-/TRAMP mice, providing no human data on prostate cancer incidence.

validated_results.title: Multi-institutional prostate cancer study of genetic susceptibility in populations of African descent.
validated_results.reason: The report centers on a genotype-stratified or gene-exposure interaction, which this protocol excludes.

validated_results.title: Re: Liu et al.: Association between manganese superoxide dismutase gene polymorphism and risk of prostate cancer: a meta-analysis (Urology 2009;74:884).
validated_results.reason: This is a correspondence letter commenting on a published meta-analysis of manganese superoxide dismutase polymorphism, with no original study results.

validated_results.title: Zinc status of patients with benign prostatic hyperplasia and prostate carcinoma.
validated_results.journal: Indian journal of urology : IJU : journal of the Urological Society of India
validated_results.reason: Tissue, plasma, and urine zinc were measured only in patients already diagnosed with prostate carcinoma or BPH, so the exposure follows diagnosis and no incidence estimate is possible.

validated_results.title: Computer aided screening of inhibitors to 5-α reductase type 2 for prostate cancer.
validated_results.reason: This is an in silico computer-aided docking screen of berberine binding to 5-alpha reductase with no human participants or incidence data.

validated_results.title: Polyphenol rich botanicals used as food supplements interfere with EphA2-ephrinA1 system.
validated_results.reason: Green tea and other plant extracts were tested only in ELISA binding assays and PC3 prostate cancer cell lines, providing no human incidence data.

validated_results.title: Polyphenol rich botanicals used as food supplements interfere with EphA2-ephrinA1 system.
validated_results.reason: Tea extract effects on the EphA2-ephrinA1 system were assessed exclusively in cell-free assays and prostate cancer cell lines without human participants.

validated_results.title: The dietary flavonol fisetin enhances the apoptosis-inducing potential of TRAIL in prostate cancer cells.
validated_results.reason: Fisetin was studied only in LNCaP, DU145, and PC3 prostate cancer cell lines for apoptosis endpoints, with no human incidence outcome.
